text: New to the city or just new to this part of it?

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: narrator
text: \"New to the city. Still finding my feet.\"

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: Then this is a good first beach. Locals mostly use it. The tourist one's two bays over - noisier, worse coffee, everyone's performing.

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: How long have you been here?

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: Long enough to find the beach, not long enough to know anyone. That's the good window, actually. Before the city starts feeling small.

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: narrator
text: \"New to this neighborhood. Still working out the city.\"

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: It has a trick to it. Took me a year before I stopped getting turned around by the waterfront.

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: Pick a direction and walk until something's worth drawing. That's my method. It's not efficient, but it works.

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: narrator
text: She seems satisfied you're not about to be annoying.

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: You're not the type who talks just to fill silence?

label: zoe_beach_approach
speaker: Zoe
text: Good. Pull up some sand if you want. I've got ten more minutes of light.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: You hang back. She's in that specific kind of concentration where interrupting would be like tripping a cable mid-charge. You know that state. You respect it.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: A few minutes go by. The water's good out here. There's a container ship on the horizon - absurdly large, barely moving.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: She erases something. Makes a short frustrated sound, almost inaudible. Re-draws the line. Erases it again.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: Her shoulders drop slightly. There's something she's trying to get that isn't coming.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: Five minutes. Maybe more. Long enough that you stop counting.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: She stretches - rolls her neck, sets the charcoal down on the sketchbook - and turns to look at the water.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: A long pause. She looks at you, then back at the water, then at you again.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: ...You've been standing there this whole time.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: I would have heard you leave.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: You were going to eventually. Everyone does.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: \"You were getting somewhere. I could see it from here.\"

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: She blinks. Looks at the sketchbook. Then back at you.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: ...I wasn't, actually. But that's the right thing to look for.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: Most people don't think about that.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: Sit down. You're making me self-conscious.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: \"You looked like you were in it.\"

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: I was. I'm not anymore. Something I was chasing got away from me.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: She doesn't sound angry. Just honest about it.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: You can come over. Since you've been hovering.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: [[Say nothing. Just hold up a hand - caught, fair enough.]]

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: She stares at you for a second. Then a short exhale. Almost a laugh.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: Come sit. You're going to get a crick in your neck standing like that.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: You cross the sand and sit down next to her. She goes back to the page, or pretends to.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: The sea does that thing where it sounds like breathing.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: What do you see? In the water.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: It's a test. You can feel it.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: Nobody looks at that. They look at the waves or the horizon. The interesting part's always in the middle somewhere.

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: narrator
text: \"Just water. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.\"

label: zoe_beach_watch
speaker: Zoe
text: The water's fine. It's what it does to everything around it that matters. But that comes with practice.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: Eventually she closes the sketchbook. Taps it twice with one charcoal-stained finger like she's filing the whole session away.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: Zoe
text: It's the right one. The other two are for people who want to be seen at the beach. This one's for people who actually want the beach.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: She starts brushing sand from her jeans. There's charcoal on two fingers. She doesn't bother with it.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: Zoe
text: I'm here most weeks when it's not raining. Trying to get the reflections right before the season changes and the light goes flat.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: She tucks the sketchbook under her arm and stands.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: Zoe
text: You're not the worst person to run into.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: She says it the way someone gives a verdict. Which, you think, she basically did.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: The smile that follows - half-turned away, like she didn't sign off on it - happens anyway.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: She walks off down the shore.

label: zoe_beach_shared
speaker: narrator
text: You think: {i}that one's going to be interesting.{/i}

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: The café looks different at this hour. Chairs stacked on half the tables. One lamp above the counter. The espresso machine, finally, quiet.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: Closing time. Lucky for you there's one cup left in the pot. Come in or don't.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She doesn't wait for an answer - pours two cups, sets them on a table, sits down. You sit across from her.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: It always is, after a shift. Time does something weird behind the counter.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"I was hoping you'd still be here.\"

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: You've been in a lot lately. What are you actually looking for in this city?

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"Money, mostly. And something that doesn't feel like wasted time.\"

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: Yeah. That's most people. They just don't say it out loud.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: Same, honestly. I've been figuring it out for three years and counting.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She wraps both hands tighter around the cup.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: I was supposed to be studying nursing right now. Deferred a year. Then another. Henry offered me full-time and the timing just... worked.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: I'm good at this job. That's the annoying part. When you're bad at something it's easy to leave.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"Then go. You're clearly just waiting for permission.\"

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"Being good at something isn't a reason to stay stuck in it.\"

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She says it quietly, like she's testing the idea.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: It's late and I live close.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: You can tell me what you're running from on the way.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She puts on her coat. Keys in hand. She looks around the café for a second - the habit of checking everything before she leaves.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: You're easier to talk to when there's no counter in the way.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She unlocks the door, holds it open.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: Don't tell Henry I gave away his last coffee.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: The café lights go off as you step outside.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She stops walking. Just for a second.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: Nora
text: That's a thing to say in the dark.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She says it lightly. The door is still open, in more ways than one.

label: nora_closing_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She doesn't try to fill it. Neither do you.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She doesn't head toward the main strip. She turns the other way, past the pier, where the sand gets quieter.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: Come on. I'll show you the actual beach.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: Nobody comes this far down. Which is exactly the point.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She drops onto a rock and kicks off her sandals. The water out here is the same water, but it feels different without the noise behind it.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: I come here when I need to not be anywhere specific, you know?

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: Every Wednesday I can manage. Some weeks it's the only thing that feels like mine.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She looks at you sideways. Not offended. Considering.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: Not running. Just... not arriving yet. There's a difference.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: Back home everyone always asks what I'm doing with my life. Out here nobody knows I exist.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She says it like it's a relief, not a complaint.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"What are you actually doing with your life?\"

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: Currently? Sitting on a rock, avoiding that exact question. You're terrible at this.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She's smiling when she says it.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"Sounds like you needed to disappear for a while.\"

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: A pause. The sea fills it better than words would.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She looks at you properly for the first time since you sat down.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You sit there without saying much. The light goes gold and orange.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: We should do something normal sometime. Not a beach. Something where we have to actually talk.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: Elle
text: If you want it to be.

label: elle_pier_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You head back through the city.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: The stairwell door is already propped open. You weren't planning to come up here — but the ward feels impossible right now and the sky is the only ceiling that isn't fluorescent.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: I figured someone else would come up eventually.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She has a paper cup of something. She doesn't look like a doctor right now. She looks like someone who's been at it too long.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: Twelve beds, two residents calling in. Standard chaos.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She says it flat. Not complaining — just cataloguing.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"I didn't know this was up here.\"

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: Most people don't bother finding out. The view's not worth it unless you need it to be.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You sit on the ledge beside her. The city is quiet at this hour in a way it never is from ground level.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: You did well tonight, by the way. That tachycardia in bed seven — you caught it before I did.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: I keep thinking I'll get used to it. The nights where you can't actually fix anything.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She's looking out at the city, not at you.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: You just manage. Make it slightly less bad. Go home. Come back.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: It is. But you don't say that out loud usually.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: Ask me on a good day and I'll say yes immediately.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: Ask me at 3am after a shift like tonight and I'll tell you I don't know.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"You're not just managing. You're very good at this.\"

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She glances at you. Something shifts in her expression.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: That's... actually something I needed to hear tonight. Thank you.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She finishes whatever's in the cup. Sets it down. Looks at the city like she's still processing something she saw eight hours ago.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: I chose this. I want to be clear about that. I'm not here by accident.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: I just didn't account for what it costs.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She stands, smooths her jacket, picks up the cup.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: Get some sleep. You're back in seven hours.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She heads for the door. Stops.

label: lena_rooftop_scene
speaker: Dr. Lena
text: It helps. Having someone up here who gets it.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You pull out the metal detector. Eli watches like they're deciding whether to take this seriously.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: Does that thing actually find anything?

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: I'm already surprised you own this.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You sweep the shoreline. Eli walks alongside, not helping exactly, but present.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: There's a rhythm to it — step, sweep, listen.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: First hit: a 2009 euro coin, warped from salt.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You toss it back into the sand for the next person.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: A second hit — louder. Eli stops talking.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You dig. A key, old enough that you can't tell what it opened.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: Someone lost that and had a very bad day.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: A pause. The sea is unhelpfully indifferent.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: I've never thought about how many things just... stay in the ground. Permanently lost.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: Third hit. Strong. Different frequency from the others.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You dig for a minute. Something metallic, small. You pull it out.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: They take it carefully. Look at it.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: There's probably no one to give this back to.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: I feel like we're supposed to feel something about this.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You both look at it for a moment.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You put it on top of a nearby rock. It won't be there tomorrow. But it's not yours.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: You pack the detector away. The light is going orange. Eli sits on the sand.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: Eli
text: I'd been meaning to say — you're easier to be around than I expected. At the start.

label: eli_find_scene
speaker: narrator
text: Eli nods once. Conversation apparently complete.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: Martha suggested this place. End of quarter, she said. Good enough reason.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: The rooftop bar is the kind of place that costs more than it shows.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She's already there. Different from the office — not looser exactly. Less constructed.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She says it like she wasn't entirely sure you would.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: I gave you a postcode and a floor number.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"I almost went to the wrong bar.\"

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: There are three on this block. It's a recurring problem.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: Drinks. The city from above. She's looking at something middle-distance.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: I wanted to say something I can't say in the office.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: You've been handled badly there. By a few people. Before you were established.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: I noticed. I didn't always act on it. I wanted you to know I noticed.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: Because you're past the point where it can be used against you.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She says it practically. The kindness is in the timing.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She looks briefly uncomfortable with the gratitude.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: Don't. Just — don't let it happen to the next person.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: Halfway through the second drink, the city gets louder and she gets quieter.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: I had a plan when I joined Nexus. Very specific. Five years.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: The work kept being interesting. I kept being good at it.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: Those two things are harder to walk away from than I planned for.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: Martha
text: Ask me in another nine years.

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: \"I think you like it more than you admit.\"

label: martha_rooftop_scene
speaker: narrator
text: She looks at you for a moment.

speaker: narrator

speaker: narrator

label: summer_festival_blackout_group
speaker: narrator

speaker: narrator
text: It turns out a crowd in the dark is mostly a crowd making jokes.

speaker: Zoe

speaker: Zoe

speaker: narrator

speaker: Eli

speaker: narrator

speaker: narrator

speaker: narrator

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Stall owners are throwing tarpaulins. Somebody's paper plate becomes a hat and then, immediately, doesn't.

speaker: Zoe

speaker: narrator
text: You end up crushed under the canopy of a closed hardware shop with about forty other people, four of whom you came with.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The rain hits the awning like applause.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator

speaker: Nora
text: My shoes are a swimming pool.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Marcus
text: Your shoes are a swimming pool that's fine.

speaker: Eli
text: The power outage and the rain are probably related.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: Pressure drop, wind ahead of the front, something moved that shouldn't have. It's the sort of thing that happens forty minutes before rain rather than during it.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: We could have known if any of us had looked up.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: You are still holding the keyring.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Marcus

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The conversation goes the way conversations go when everyone's damp and slightly tired and nobody has anywhere to be.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Somebody two metres away is telling a stranger their entire job history. Somebody else has produced a bag of crisps for forty people.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Nora
text: This is the good part, by the way.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: [mc_name]
text: The standing under an awning part?

speaker: Nora

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The group drifts into pairs, the way it does. There's a gap next to each of them.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Marcus is quieter than he's been all night.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: He's watching the stage end of the street, where the band is sitting on the edge of the trailer with their instruments in bin bags.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Marcus
text: They're going to go back on.

speaker: Marcus

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Marcus

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: He says it lightly and then doesn't say anything else, which for Marcus is the whole story.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Eli has gone quiet in an interesting way.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Eli is looking out at the rain running off the awning in a single unbroken sheet.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: I've been avoiding a chapter for six weeks.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: Seven weeks, then. I'm rounding down.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: The thing I keep getting stuck on is that all of this is measurable. Crowd density, load on the supply, drainage on this street. Somebody modelled all of it. Probably badly.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: And nobody standing here cares, and it worked anyway.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: That's supposed to be reassuring. I haven't decided if it is.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: [mc_name]
text: You don't have to decide tonight.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: No. That's the part I'm bad at.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Zoe's watching the rain with that look she gets.

speaker: narrator
text: She's not looking at the rain. She's looking at the light in it — the one string of bulbs still lit somewhere up the street, coming apart in the water.

speaker: Zoe
text: That's the thing I've been trying to get out of the waterfront pieces for four months.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: It's not the reflection. It's that you can't tell where the light stops being the light.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: She doesn't take a photo. She doesn't reach for a sketchbook.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: It doesn't translate. That's the entire point of it.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: I'll remember it wrong in about a week and paint that instead. That's usually better anyway.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Nora is laughing at something and it makes the whole awning lighter.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Someone has given her half a very bad pastry and she is reviewing it out loud to a stranger, at length, without mercy.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Nora
text: — and it's not underbaked, that's the thing, it's {i}confidently{/i} underbaked —

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The stranger is delighted. Two more people have moved closer to listen.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: She catches you watching and stops.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: [mc_name]
text: You're going to be good at the course.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: That lands somewhere. She looks at the pastry instead of at you.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Nora
text: I'm going to be terrible at it for about a year.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: She takes another bite of the bad pastry. She doesn't say thank you out loud.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Marcus
text: Right — someone find out if that band's going back on.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: They're going back on. Look at them.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Nora
text: Ten minutes. They'll want the rain to stop being the story.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The rain starts being less of a story.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The bulbs over the road come up first, one string at a time, in the wrong order.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Half the street stays dark. Nobody minds. It looks better.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The staff member from earlier goes past, spots you, and gives you a thumbs up that is about seventy percent relief.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: [mc_name]
text: Probably for the guy with the meter.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: It was for you. He looked directly at you.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Whoever finally sorted it doesn't come out to be looked at. That's usually how it goes.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: You were closer than the first three people who tried.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Nobody comes out to explain what happened. The lights are on, so the question stops existing.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: About a third of the crowd has gone home. The third that's left is the third that was always going to stay.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The band goes back on. Three songs, no lighting rig, and the sound is worse and better at the same time.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: Everyone told you. You just said it loudest.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The stalls come down faster than they went up. Trestle tables folding, cable being coiled by someone who is clearly not being paid enough to coil it properly.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The street starts being a street again.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Nora
text: Text me when you get in. Not because anything's going to happen to you. Just do it.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Nora
text: This was better than it had any right to be. Somebody should have organised it worse.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: She goes. She's dry from the knees up and completely soaked below, and she's not going to mention it again.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: I'm walking. It's twenty minutes and I want to look at the wet buildings.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: [mc_name]
text: That's a real sentence you just said.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: It's the best sentence I've said all week.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: I'm walking. The light's still doing the thing.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Zoe
text: I'll show you the wrong version. When it exists.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: She goes up the street rather than down it, which is the long way, which is obviously the point.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: I have a chapter and now I have a reason not to open it, which is a better position than I was in this morning.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Eli pauses at the edge of the awning.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: Thank you for not telling me to just write it.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Eli
text: That was the plan and now it's the schedule.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: Marcus turns the keyring over in his hand once and puts it back in his pocket.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: That's the whole conversation and it's enough for him.

speaker: Marcus
text: You disappeared into a dark alley to look at a fuse box for a street party. On a Friday.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: Marcus
text: Knock if you need anything. Standing offer, still stands.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: He walks the fifty metres home that you're also walking, which he does not comment on, and neither do you.

label: summer_festival_post_blackout
speaker: narrator
text: The barricades are already coming off the top of the road. Somebody's sweeping.

speaker: narrator

speaker: narrator
text: Spent an evening at the Downtown Summer Festival with Marcus, Eli, Zoe and Nora.

label: tr_first_day
speaker: narrator
text: You shadow Kai for the 7am session — a regular, mid-40s, been training here two years.

label: tr_first_day
speaker: narrator
text: She barely speaks during the session. She cues, adjusts, watches. The client barely notices the adjustments.

label: tr_first_day
speaker: narrator
text: \"Their left shoulder was compensating on the press.\"

label: tr_first_day
speaker: Kai
text: Yes. They've been doing it eight months. I'm working it out slowly — if I correct it too fast, they'll stop trusting the process.

label: tr_first_day
speaker: Kai
text: The talking is in the adjustments. If you're narrating everything, they stop feeling what's happening.

label: tr_first_day
speaker: Kai
text: Two years. But comfort isn't automatic — you maintain it. Every session.

label: tr_first_day
speaker: Kai
text: That's the first thing to understand.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: Kai
text: New client. Intake form says general fitness, weight loss, no injury history. It's yours. I'll be on the floor.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: The client is twenty-three, gym-anxious, talks a lot when nervous.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: During the assessment you discover they haven't done structured exercise before. 'Some gym experience' meant the treadmill, twice.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: Adjust the plan on the spot — start simpler than the intake suggests.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: You rebuild the session mentally while they talk. Bodyweight first. Lower the stakes.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: They finish looking surprised at themselves.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: Kai
text: You read them right. The plan matters less than the first experience.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: Stick to the plan — they said they had experience.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: The session works mechanically. They complete it. They're quiet at the end.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: Kai
text: The form was what they wished was true. What did the actual session tell you?

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: Check in mid-session: ask them how they're finding it.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: narrator
text: They tell you. You adjust. The session shifts into something they can stay with.

label: tr_task_1
speaker: Kai
text: Good. Asking mid-session is harder than adjusting upfront. You made them feel like it was their decision.

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: narrator
text: Between sessions, Kai walks you through a client's twelve-week plan.

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: Kai
text: Why three days a week and not four?

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: narrator
text: \"Recovery. Three days gives enough time between sessions.\"

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: Kai
text: That's the technical answer. What's the real answer?

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: Kai
text: Four days means four choices to come. Three means the choice is smaller. For a first-year client, compliance is the programme.

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: narrator
text: She explains the compliance reasoning. Three minutes. By the end you have a different understanding of what periodization actually does.

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: narrator
text: \"I don't know — what's the right answer?\"

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: narrator
text: She walks through the logic without condescension. The plan becomes legible.

label: tr_npc1_kai
speaker: Kai
text: Programming isn't just physical. It's a conversation about what they can sustain.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: Your last client of the day kept their session — third rebook after two cancellations.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: They were quiet throughout. Not focused-quiet — somewhere-else quiet.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: After they leave, Kai is still on the floor. She saw the session.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: She doesn't add to it immediately.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: Kai
text: The training is the easy part. Anyone can count reps. The rest is whether you stay interested in the person.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: Kai
text: Today you kept the session consistent. That was the right call — they needed the routine.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: \"I wasn't sure what to do in there.\"

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: Kai
text: You kept it professional and let them set the pace. When someone needs the hour to be normal, normal is the thing you give them.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: \"Is this always part of the job?\"

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: Kai
text: The physical stuff is what gets people through the door. The rest is why you either stay in this career or you don't.

label: tr_npc2_kai
speaker: narrator
text: She says it without drama. Like it's a fact she's made her peace with.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: Your 9am is a regular — twelve sessions in, trains for recreational half-marathons.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: They arrive moving carefully. Before the warm-up finishes, they stop.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: They have a charity run in nine days.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: Kai is at the other end of the floor with her own client.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: Stop the session and refer to a physio.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: [mc_name]
text: We're not training on that today.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: [mc_name]
text: Sharp knee pain before a warm-up is your body asking to be heard.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: [mc_name]
text: I'd refer you to a physio before we touch another session. Nine days is enough time for an assessment.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: They don't look happy. They look relieved.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: Modify to pain-free movement and document it.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: [mc_name]
text: We're not going anywhere near that range of motion today.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: You rebuild the session: upper body, seated core, nothing that loads the knee past ninety degrees.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: You write it down — pain onset, location, what you avoided and why.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: The client finishes looking surprised the hour was still useful.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: Continue carefully — the client knows their body.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: [mc_name]
text: We'll take it easy. Listen to the signals.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: Halfway through the session the catching becomes a catch-and-lock.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: You stop immediately, but the session ends early.

label: tr_boundary_case
speaker: narrator
text: The client limps slightly on the way to the changing room.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: The referred client returns with a physio report and a revised training plan.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: Iliotibial band — tightness compounding over their mileage increase. Three weeks modified; back to full in four to six.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: The plan they bring you is more specific than the one you had.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: Kai
text: The ones who think there's a grey zone there are the ones I watch.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: The client has been back twice since. The documentation you wrote became the basis for their revised plan.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: Kai
text: Your notes were clear. That matters — if anything had developed, the chain was there.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: [mc_name]
text: I wasn't sure it was enough at the time.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: Kai
text: That's why you wrote it down.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: Two sessions cancelled without rescheduling. A message this morning.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: 'Pain got worse after the gym session. Seeing a doctor. Not sure about the rest of the programme.'

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: [mc_name]
text: I made the wrong call. They said the pain was sharp and I let them continue.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: Kai doesn't fill the silence right away.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: [mc_name]
text: Stop the session. Refer. Regardless of what they wanted.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: Kai
text: Knowing what you'd change is the start of not making the same call again.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: [mc_name]
text: They insisted. I modified the intensity. I didn't think it would escalate.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: narrator
text: She looks at the floor. Not angry — deliberate.

label: tr_boundary_followup
speaker: Kai
text: We'll keep working. But this goes into how I think about your progression.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: The knee client — that referral was the right call. That kind of judgment is the last thing I can teach in a timeline.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: The documentation on the knee session — that's professional practice. Most people either ignore it or overcorrect. You found the line.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: The knee session. You got it wrong and said so. That's harder than getting it right in the first place.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: We've covered the knee session. Your reasoning at the time still concerns me. I need to see you think differently under that kind of pressure.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: Morning slot, Monday to Friday — yours. Your own client book starts Monday. Trainer, effective immediately.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: You adjusted to your clients instead of adjusting your clients to a plan. That's the one thing I can't teach in a timeline.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: You own the relationship from intake to programme review. No checking with me — your call, your accountability.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: I'm available. But you're not asking permission anymore.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: Kai
text: You earned the slot. I moved the paperwork.

label: tr_review_asst
speaker: narrator
text: She sounds like she means it.

label: wev_tr_challenging_client
speaker: narrator
text: Your 10am client wants to go heavier than their programme calls for. They've been pushing for two sessions.

label: wev_tr_challenging_client
speaker: narrator
text: Hold the line — explain the reason clearly.

label: wev_tr_challenging_client
speaker: narrator
text: You explain progressive overload. They listen, not entirely convinced.

label: wev_tr_challenging_client
speaker: narrator
text: You hold the programme. They come back next week.

label: wev_tr_challenging_client
speaker: narrator
text: Give them one heavier set at the end as a concession.

label: wev_tr_challenging_client
speaker: narrator
text: One set, controlled, to acknowledge the goal.
